description: Compare 2 to 5 ecommerce brands side by side in ONE call, as observed by StackEnhance Signal: current frequency (average marketing emails per week, last 90 days), emails observed in the last 6 months, the date Signal first observed each brand, the latest campaign date, and each brand's rank in its market when it has one, ordered by frequency. Use this instead of calling get_brand_summary repeatedly when the user names a set of brands: "Compare Mio, IKEA and Westwing", "Who emails more, Boozt or Zalando?", "How does Newport compare with its competitors?". Pass the brand names as the user wrote them, as plain strings (objects {"name", "market"} are accepted too). Give `market` (SE, NO, DK, FI, DE or a country name) when the user names a country, which is the usual case. Without a market, brands tracked in several countries are compared in the market where most of the set is tracked (Sweden first on a tie) and the answer says which, so you do not need to ask the user first; give `market` only to compare another country. Optionally give `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM-DD, starting within the last six months) to also count each brand's sends in that period. More than 5 brands: call again with the rest. To discover competitors first, use find_brands. Returns aggregates only: no campaign list, subject lines, offers or creative analysis. There is no open, click or revenue data. Cite each brand's details_url as the source.

market.description: Country for this brand only, e.g. "SE".

brands.description: 2 to 5 brand names as the user wrote them, e.g. ["Mio", "IKEA", "Westwing"]. Objects like {"name": "Mio", "market": "SE"} are accepted too.

from.description: Optional first day of a period to also count, YYYY-MM-DD.

market.description: Country the brands are in, as a two-letter code (SE, NO, DK, FI, DE) or its name ("Sweden"). Not a topic or category.

to.description: Optional last day of that period, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD.

name: compare_brands
title: Compare brands by email frequency
